result.title: LVS: Local View Synthesis from Relative Camera Pose by Reusing Previous Views
result.summary: Interactive scene exploration requires frequent view updates, although small camera motions preserve much of the visible content. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting nevertheless renders each target view, leaving this image overlap unexploited. Reusing rendered images offers an alternative. Geometric warping alone cannot recover newly exposed content and remains sensitive to depth errors. We propose a per-scene framework that replaces repeated scene rendering for nearby views with relative-pose-guided RGB-D image reuse. Geometric warping uses depth and relative pose to transport source content, while a lightweight multiscale network predicts RGB residuals to correct artifacts and infer missing appearance. Cached source features further reduce repeated computation. On GS-render, residual refinement improves PSNR by 0.72~dB over pure warping; evaluations on captured and rendered scenes demonstrate low query latency. This separation of scene rendering from local view updates supports responsive scene exploration, with potential applications in augmented and virtual reality.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种逐场景框架，用相对位姿引导的 RGB-D 图像复用与多尺度残差网络替代 3D Gaussian Splatting 对邻近视角的重复渲染，以降低交互式视角更新延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于 3DGS 视角合成与图像渲染效率方向，与 VLM 推理状态、视觉证据筛选、latent 生成或停止决策无实质联系；「复用上一视角」与特征缓存虽表面近似 latent 缓存，但目标是渲染加速而非推理，未提供可核查的迁移线索。
